name: containerize-aspnet-framework
description: Containerize an ASP.NET .NET Framework project for Windows Docker.

Scope: Change only what is required for containerization. This is .NET Framework, not .NET Core. ❌ No infrastructure setup (assumed to be handled separately). ❌ No code changes beyond those required for containerization.

Settings (unspecified values use bracketed defaults):
- Project: `[ProjectName (provide path to .csproj file)]`
- Windows Server SKU: `[Windows Server Core (Default) or Windows Server Full]`; version: unspecified.
- Build base image: `[Specify base image to use for build stage (Default None)]`; run base image: `[Specify base image to use for run stage (Default None)]`.
- Primary HTTP port: `[e.g., 80]`; additional ports: `[List any additional ports, or "None"]`.
- Container user: `[User account, or default to "ContainerUser"]`; IIS settings: `[List any specific IIS settings, or "None"]`.
- Before/after build steps: `[List any specific build steps, or "None"]` each.
- GAC assemblies: `[Assembly name and version, or "None"]`; MSIs: `[MSI names and versions, or "None"]`; COM: `[COM component names, or "None"]`.
- Registry: `[Registry paths and values, or "None"]`; environment: `[Variable names and values, or "Use defaults"]`; roles/features: `[Role/feature names, or "None"]`.
- Copy: `[Paths relative to project root, or "None"]` to `[Container paths, or "Not applicable"]`; exclude: `[Paths to exclude, or "None"]`; additional `.dockerignore` patterns: `[List any additional patterns, or "None"]`.
- Health endpoint: `[Health check URL path, or "None"]`; interval/timeout: `[Interval and timeout values, or "Use defaults"]`.
- Other instructions: `[Specific requirements, or "None"]`; known issues: `[Describe any known issues, or "None"]`.

Procedure:
1. Review settings; create `progress.md` with the checklist below. Detect .NET Framework via `TargetFrameworkVersion` in the project's .csproj; select image for framework, SKU and Windows Server version (2016, 2019, or 2022). Core tags: https://github.com/microsoft/dotnet-framework-docker/blob/main/README.aspnet.md#full-tag-listing
2. **DO NOT** install missing required NuGet packages. If missing, pause executing this prompt and ask the user to install them manually using the Visual Studio NuGet Package Manager or Visual Studio package manager console: `Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment`.
3. Modify `web.config`: add configBuilders section in configSections, root configBuilders section, and EnvironmentConfigBuilder for appSettings and connectionStrings:
`<section name="configBuilders" type="System.Configuration.ConfigurationBuildersSection, System.Configuration, Version=<REDACTED_IP>, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a" restartOnExternalChanges="false" requirePermission="false" />`
`<add name="Environment" type="Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.EnvironmentConfigBuilder, Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment" />`
`<appSettings configBuilders="Environment">`
`<connectionStrings configBuilders="Environment">`
Preserve existing settings and connection strings.
4. Create `LogMonitorConfig.json` beside Dockerfile, copying the reference contents below. The file's contents **MUST NOT** not be modified and should match the reference content exactly unless instructions in containerization settings specify otherwise. In particular, do not change EventLog issue levels to `Information`.
5. Create project-root Dockerfile with build and final stages. Build on Windows Server Core; build stage MUST use a `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/sdk` base image unless a custom base image is specified in the settings file. Copy sln, csproj, packages.config first; copy NuGet.config if present and configure private feeds; restore NuGet packages; then copy remaining source and MSBuild/publish to `C:\publish`. Final stage MUST use a `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/aspnet` base image unless a custom base image is specified in the settings file. **IMPORTANT:** Use a Windows Server Core base image unless the user has **specifically requested** a full Windows Server image in the settings file. Apply all settings, dependencies, roles, files, ports and user. Copy published output to `C:\inetpub\wwwroot`; copy `LogMonitorConfig.json` to `C:\LogMonitor`; download LogMonitor.exe there from https://github.com/microsoft/windows-container-tools/releases/download/v2.1.1/LogMonitor.exe. Set working directory to `C:\inetpub\wwwroot` and entry point:
`ENTRYPOINT [ "C:\\LogMonitor\\LogMonitor.exe", "C:\\ServiceMonitor.exe", "w3svc" ]`
6. Create project-root `.dockerignore` excluding unnecessary files, including additional specified patterns. Add HEALTHCHECK if endpoint specified. Add `<None Include="Dockerfile" />` to project file.
7. Mark tasks completed `[ ] → [✓]`; build with `docker build -t aspnet-app:latest .`; diagnose failures, adjust and report success/failure. Do not pause for confirmation between steps. Continue methodically until the application has been containerized and Docker build succeeds. **YOU ARE NOT DONE UNTIL ALL CHECKBOXES ARE MARKED!** This includes building the Docker image successfully and addressing any issues that arise during the build process.

`progress.md` checklist:
[ ] .NET Framework version detection (version: ___)
[ ] Windows Server SKU selection (SKU: ___)
[ ] Windows Server version selection (Version: ___)
[ ] Web.config modifications for configuration builders
[ ] NuGet package source configuration (if applicable)
[ ] Copy LogMonitorConfig.json and adjust if required by settings
[ ] .dockerignore file creation
[ ] Build stage created with SDK image
[ ] sln, csproj, packages.config, and (if applicable) NuGet.config copied for package restore
[ ] Runtime stage created with runtime image
[ ] Non-root user configuration
[ ] Dependency handling (GAC, MSI, COM, registry, additional files, etc.)
[ ] Health check configuration (if applicable)
[ ] Special requirements implementation
[ ] Review containerization settings and make sure that all requirements are met
[ ] Docker build success

Reference `LogMonitorConfig.json` contents:
"directory": "c:\\inetpub\\logs",
"providerName": "IIS: WWW Server",
"providerGuid": "3A2A4E84-4C21-4981-AE10-3FDA0D9B0F83",
"providerName": "Microsoft-Windows-IIS-Logging",
"providerGuid": "7E8AD27F-B271-4EA2-A783-A47BDE29143B",
